name: Potato

schedule.notes: Plant seed pieces with at least one 'eye' each, cut-side down.
Hill up to 8 in as plants grow. Tubers form on stems above seed piece.
New potatoes after flowering; storage potatoes 2 to 3 weeks after vines die back.

harvest.cues: Skin doesn't rub off easily — that's the cure indicator. For new potatoes, harvest while skins are still thin and flaky.
harvest.storageNotes: Cure 1 to 2 weeks at 60 F dark, then store at 38 to 45 F dark and humid. Don't wash before storage. Keeps 4 to 6 months.

varieties.name: Russian Banana
varieties.notes: Yellow fingerling, excellent roasted. Long season.

notes: Always use certified seed potatoes — grocery-store potatoes carry disease. Hill or mulch deeply to keep tubers covered; sunlight turns them green and bitter (solanine).
